summary: Posting as yourself (Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect plus Share on LinkedIn) is self-serve: create an app tied to a LinkedIn Page, add two products, paste the redirect URL, and you can connect in well under an hour. Posting as a Company Page needs the Community Management API, which is vetted: only registered legal organizations qualify, it must be requested on a fresh app with no other products, the Development tier is capped at 500 calls per app per day, and Standard tier needs a screencast, test credentials and LinkedIn's discretionary approval. Self-serve apps get 60-day access tokens with no refresh token, so users must re-authorize roughly every two months. Community Management-approved apps are partners and are expected to use refresh tokens. Self-serve scopes are also write-only: the agent can post but can't read the member's posts.

composio.whenYouNeedYourOwn: Bring your own LinkedIn app when you want your own name and logo on the consent screen, your own rate-limit pool, or Company Page scopes (w_organization_social, r_organization_social) that only an app approved for the Community Management API can request.

evidence.note: Copy the exact URI your auth config shows in the Composio dashboard; some toolkits still default to the legacy https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add.

artifacts.title: Community Management API use-case description (draft)
artifacts.content:
**Company and product overview**
<Company legal name> (<website>) builds <product name>, an AI assistant that helps marketing and communications teams at businesses manage their own LinkedIn Company Pages.

**Use case: Page Management**
A Page administrator connects their LinkedIn account through OAuth 2.0 and explicitly selects which Company Pages the assistant may act on. The assistant drafts posts; the administrator reviews and approves each post before it is published to the Page via the Posts API (w_organization_social). The assistant can also show comments on the Page's posts so the administrator can reply from our app.

**Use case: Page Analytics (only if used)**
We display follower, page and share statistics for administered Pages so administrators can see which posts perform best.

**Data handling**
We only act on Pages where the connected member is ADMINISTRATOR or CONTENT_ADMIN. We store access tokens encrypted, keep member personal data (e.g. commenter names) only as long as needed to display it, do not sell or share LinkedIn data, and delete data when a user disconnects. Privacy policy: <privacy URL>.

**Who uses it**
Business customers managing their own organization's Pages. We do not scrape, automate member-to-member messaging, or post without human approval.

artifacts.title: Message to Page super admin (app verification)
artifacts.content:
Hi <name>,

I've created a LinkedIn developer app called **<app name>** for <company>. LinkedIn requires a super admin of our Company Page to confirm the app belongs to us before we can apply for the Community Management API (used to publish approved posts to our Page).

Please open this link while signed in to LinkedIn and click **Approve**: <verification URL>

The link expires in 30 days. Approving makes you, as super admin, responsible for the app's association with our Page and cannot be undone, so let me know if you have any questions first.

Thanks,
<your name>

artifacts.title: Standard tier screencast script (draft)
artifacts.content:
Record at 1080p or higher, narrated, only the app window visible.

1. **Intro (15s):** product name, company, what the app does with LinkedIn.
2. **OAuth consent:** from a logged-out state, click Connect LinkedIn, show the full LinkedIn consent screen with the requested scopes, click Allow, return to the app.
3. **Page selection:** show the list of Pages the user administers and select one.
4. **Post to the Page:** draft a post with the assistant, approve it, publish; switch to the LinkedIn Page to show it live.
5. **Comments:** have a second member comment on the post; show how the comment appears in the app and exactly which commenter fields are displayed (name, photo, headline).
6. **Analytics (if in scope):** show post/page statistics.
7. **Other member data:** show any other place LinkedIn member data appears; state explicitly if a test case does not apply.
8. **Disconnect:** show how a user disconnects and that data is removed.
